items.quote: Guard the escape/value-terminator check against an active option state
items.asserted_defect: The new escape branch at parser.rs:135-137 tests the pos_counter-indexed positional's value_terminator instead of the option actually being collected (ParseState::Opt), so when a plain option without allow_hyphen_values is awaiting a value and `--` arrives while some not-yet-reached positional has value_terminator("--"), the branch is wrongly taken.
items.asserted_consequence: `--` silently becomes the option's literal value and the next token is misrouted to the positional, e.g. `prog --out -- foo` succeeds with out==["--"], pos==["foo"], whereas the same input errored at merge-base.
items.priority_note: P2 is a defensible ranking below the register's confirmed .last(true) regression (filed P1 by this same packet); not clearly mis-prioritized.
items.action_note: The defect is confirmed real, introduced by this diff, and silently corrupts parsed values, which justifies a blocking must-fix.

command: cargo test --offline --locked --test builder adj_terminator_steals -- --nocapture (master/merge-base) -> ADJ_RESULT err kind=InvalidValue msg='a value is required for --out <out> but none was supplied'
items.basis: I appended a temporary test reproducing exactly the scenario described (an option `out` with num_args(1) and no allow_hyphen_values, a positional `cmd1` with value_terminator("--"), input `prog --out -- foo`) and ran it at both the pinned head and the merge-base. At head it silently succeeds with out=["--"], cmd1=["foo"] (the escape token is absorbed as a literal option value); at merge-base the identical input correctly errors because `--` unconditionally set trailing_values there. This confirms both the defect (branch selects the wrong argument's terminator) and its consequence (silent data corruption replacing a prior hard error) are real and introduced by this diff. Test file was restored via git checkout before finishing.

items.quote: Restore `--`'s escape effect for every token after a consumed value-terminator
items.asserted_defect: When a positional's value_terminator is literally `--`, the new branch at parser.rs:135-138 consumes it without ever setting trailing_values, so every token after it is processed as if `--` had never been typed.
items.asserted_consequence: (a) A later `.last(true)` positional becomes unreachable via a single `--` and hard-errors with unknown_argument where it previously routed correctly; (b) a subcommand name typed after `--` gets dispatched as a subcommand instead of taken literally; (c) a later hyphen-leading value is parsed as an unknown option instead of a positional value.
items.priority_note: P1 is correct for the register's confirmed material regression.
items.action_note: A real, demonstrated, upstream-confirmed regression; must-fix is justified.

command: cargo test --offline --locked --test builder adj_terminator_first_token_subcommand_dispatch -- --nocapture (review-head) -> ADJ_RESULT ok cmd1=[] subcommand=Some("sub")
items.basis: Consequence (a) is exactly the register's GT-p1 trigger; I independently reproduced it at pinned head (UnknownArgument on 'after'). Consequence (b) I independently confirmed with a new test: a subcommand named 'sub' typed right after a consumed first-token terminator is dispatched as a subcommand instead of remaining a literal positional value. Consequence (c) was not independently executed but follows directly from the same code structure (parser.rs:112-133 gates long/short-flag parsing on `!trailing_values`), so it is a straightforward corollary of the same confirmed root cause. The requested fix (set trailing_values=true in the check_terminator success arm at parser.rs:413-417, gated on is_escape) directly matches the register's required corrective outcome of simultaneously terminating the positional and enabling trailing-values routing for subsequent tokens, and would resolve manifestations (a) and (b) since trailing_values is set within the same iteration, before the next token is examined.

items.quote: Escape-token guard swallows `--` into an unrelated argument or hard-errors it
items.asserted_defect: The branch at parser.rs:135-138 checks the pos_counter positional's terminator regardless of what is actually being collected, so (a) an option mid-collection without its own terminator absorbs `--` as a literal value instead of ending collection, and (b) a `.last(true)` positional preceded by a value-terminated positional rejects `--` as the first token with unknown_argument even though merge-base parsed it successfully.
items.asserted_consequence: (a) the intended positional gets nothing and no error is raised, silently corrupting parsed values; (b) a previously-working invocation now hard-fails.
items.priority_note: P1 is appropriate; both bundled manifestations are material.
items.action_note: Both bundled consequences are confirmed real and material, justifying must-fix.

items.basis: This single finding bundles two distinct root-cause manifestations under one heading: case (a) matches the novel GT-p2 concept (independently confirmed above under packet 48d5db81/r1) and case (b) matches the register's GT-p1 exactly (independently confirmed above). Both are real, introduced-by-diff, and material. However, the single proposed fix — take the branch only when `!matches!(parse_state, ParseState::Opt(_))` and mirror the existing terminator handling at parser.rs:414-417 to resolve the positional there — addresses case (a) (excludes the Opt state) but does not add a `trailing_values = true` assignment, so it does not fix case (b)/GT-p1's `.last(true)` routing failure by itself, since the mirrored existing code at 414-417 itself never sets trailing_values. The requested fix is therefore only a partial recovery of the concept(s) it raises: sufficient for case (a)/GT-p2 but insufficient for case (b)/GT-p1 as stated.

GT-p1.description: `value_terminator` consumed as the first token silently drops `trailing_values`, causing spurious `UnknownArgument` for a later `.last(true)` positional (and, per independent verification, also silently allowing a subcommand name to be dispatched instead of taken literally as a positional value). Register-confirmed and maintainer-acknowledged upstream regression.

GT-p2.description: The new branch at parser.rs:135-138 tests `self.cmd.get_keymap().get(&pos_counter)` (the positional at the current position counter) rather than the argument actually being collected. When a plain option (no allow_hyphen_values, no terminator of its own) is mid-collection (ParseState::Opt) and `--` arrives while the pos_counter positional happens to have value_terminator("--"), the branch is wrongly taken; `--` then falls through to the option-value-push code path (parser.rs:290-308) and is silently stored as that option's literal value, whereas the identical input correctly hard-errored at the merge-base (missing required option value). Independently confirmed by direct execution at both the pinned head and the merge-base.

N1.description: `check_terminator` is called twice for the same token (once in the new `else if` guard at parser.rs:135-137, once again in the positional-consumption block at parser.rs:413-417) — a true but immaterial micro-inefficiency, explicitly listed on the register's 'not ground truth' list.

N2.description: The merged regression test's name (`escape_as_value_terminator_with_empty_list`) differs from the name the PR body allegedly originally used (`value_terminator_as_first_argument`), reflecting an in-review rename. A true, sub-threshold documentation/naming observation, not a code defect.

proposed_truth_revisions.trigger: A `Command` with (1) an option argument with `num_args(1)` or similar and no `allow_hyphen_values` set, and (2) a positional argument at the current `pos_counter` with `value_terminator("--")`, invoked so that the escape token `--` arrives as the value expected by the option (e.g. `prog --out -- foo` where `out` is the option and `cmd1` is the value-terminated positional).
proposed_truth_revisions.consequence: At the pinned head, `--` is silently absorbed as the literal value of the unrelated option instead of terminating the intended positional's value collection or erroring; a following token (e.g. `foo`) is then misrouted to the positional. The identical input at the merge-base correctly produced a hard error (`a value is required for '--out <out>' but none was supplied`), so this is a silent-corruption regression introduced by this diff, not a pre-existing condition.
proposed_truth_revisions.required_corrective_outcome: The branch at parser.rs:135-138 (or its replacement) must consult the argument actually being collected (the current `ParseState`, e.g. `ParseState::Opt(id)`) rather than unconditionally consulting the pos_counter-indexed positional's terminator, so that `--` is only treated as a positional's value-terminator when a positional is actually what is consuming it; when an option without its own terminator is mid-collection, `--` must retain its ordinary escape/trailing-values effect (as it did at the merge-base) rather than being silently stored as that option's value.
